sources.text:
After Deadly Shooting at Bend Elementary School, Catholic Bishops Call for Prayer
Oregon Catholic bishops are urging prayer after a tragic shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, on Oct. 15 that left five people dead — including three young children — and two critically wounded.
According to Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz, a 16-year-old forced his way into the elementary school by shooting through locked doors before opening fire inside. The gunman killed three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, alongside a teacher, before he was shot and killed at the scene by a bystander who had spotted him entering the building. A 7-year-old student and another teacher were rushed to a local hospital with critical injuries.
A teacher who was in a classroom on campus during the entire ordeal, Kathy Sheil Smith, spoke with CNN affiliate KPTV on Thursday night, saying of the students, “They were so afraid. The looks on their faces was really hard to see.”
Speaking to what occurred on the ground, she saw the shooter enter the school from her classroom window. After alerting the main office, she moved her students to a corner of the classroom to shelter in place. “Some kids were praying; some kids were consoling other kids,” Smith said.
As shots were heard across the school, she said some teachers imagined they wouldn’t make it out alive.
“I’m sure that every teacher at the school thought, ‘Today is the day that I am going to die,’” she said through tears.
The tragedy has prompted an outpouring of pastoral care and community support across the state, with hundreds attending a candelight vigil last night.
“We expect that our schools are safe places for our children and all who pass through their doors. When a tragedy like this occurs, it shakes us to our core,” wrote Bishop Thomas Hennen of the Diocese of Baker — which encompasses the city of Bend — in an Oct. 15 letter offering his “heartfelt prayers for those whose lives were taken in the shooting.”
Acknowledging the overwhelming wave of emotions confronting the city, Bishop Hennen pointed to faith, solidarity and action as the path forward.
“It is only natural that we would be flooded with emotions at a time like this — shock, grief, fear, confusion, anger,” Bishop Hennen wrote. “Even as more is known about what happened, there are no adequate answers for why this happened. We can only mourn, support each other, and pledge ourselves to doing everything in our power to prevent such tragedies in the future.”
The prelate said the entire “Catholic community of central and eastern Oregon mourns with the families of the victims, the Silver Rail community and the city of Bend.”
In the immediate aftermath of the shooting, emergency responders transported surviving students and staff by bus to a nearby church, where families and guardians were reunified with their loved ones.
Speaking at an evening media briefing, Chief Krantz noted that law enforcement notified all victim families and that an active, thorough investigation remains underway. While Krantz was not immediately able to confirm the shooter’s motive, connection to the school, weapon types, or total rounds fired, police spokesperson Sheila Miller confirmed that a follow-up press conference is scheduled for the afternoon of Oct. 16.
Local officials and state leaders emphasized the need for communal healing, counseling and mutual support in the days ahead.
“In the coming days, there will be opportunities to gather, including a community vigil tonight, to mourn together, honor those affected and those lost, and begin the difficult process of healing,” said Bend Mayor Melanie Kebler.
At the state level, Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek confirmed that the Department of Emergency Management is actively coordinating resources to assist the local community.
“We must come together and support each other, neighbor to neighbor, Oregonian to Oregonian,” Kotek said.
Crisis counselors have also been mobilized across the school district to help students and families.
Archbishop Alexander Sample of the Archdiocese of Portland also issued a statement on Oct. 15, offering spiritual closeness to the grieving families and the broader community.
“No family should ever have to experience such fear and heartbreak. Please know that you are not alone,” Archbishop Sample said. “I hold you close in prayer, and the Church stands with you in this time of sorrow.”

If this is the case, then the incident may be buried by the establishment media. It might also be sent down the memory hole because of the successful intervention of an armed citizen. The narrative for decades within the media was that armed civilians rarely if ever stop violent crimes.
The Crime Prevention Research Center (CPRC) has repeatedly examined the definitions used by the FBI to categorize civilian interventions in violent crimes, and they found significantly higher numbers of such cases than the FBI had reported. In other words, the FBI was suppressing the actual data on civilians saving the day, often with their own firearms.
One recent CPRC count identified 615 active shooter incidents from 2014–2025 and concluded armed citizens stopped 225 of them (about 36.6%). When limited to locations where civilians are legally allowed to carry (i.e., excluding gun-free zones), the rate rises to roughly 52–53% (and higher in some recent single-year examples).
CPRC attributes the gap to the FBI missing or overlooking numerous incidents and occasionally misclassifying civilian interventions (for example, listing private armed citizens or volunteer church security as professional security guards). They argue their expanded list still uses the FBI’s core definition and that media coverage tends to under-emphasize successful civilian interventions.
While gun control advocates often cite mass shootings as a reason for banning of weapons (or outright confiscation), these incidents account for only 2% of all gun deaths in the US on average. The majority (around 60%) are suicides, and 35% are homicides.
Around 20% of US counties account for 90% of all homicides in the country. Of these counties, the vast majority are controlled by Democrats. Among the worst 1% of US counties (about 31 counties, holding ~20% of the population and ~41% of murders in recent data), the CPRC lists political leanings as 21 Democratic strongholds, 6 leaning Democratic, and 4 swing or Republican-leaning.
In other words, the counties with the most aggressive gun control advocates and laws in the US are also the places with the most gun violence. Perhaps it's because law abiding citizens in these places are far less likely to carry, which emboldens criminals to commit more violence.

Three children and teacher killed in Oregon primary school shooting
Tragedy strikes Silver Rail Primary School in Bend as 16-year-old gunman is shot dead within minutes of attack
T. Nieva
Bend (Oregon)
A shooting at a primary school in the US state of Oregon has left four people dead, including three children and a teacher, according to ... local authorities and US media reports. The 16-year-old suspect was found "shot dead" at the scene shortly after police arrived.
Emergency services were alerted to a critical incident at Silver Rail Primary School in the city of Bend at approximately 1.00pm local time. Officers arrived at the campus within two minutes of the initial call.
"Seconds later, we received a radio report that the suspect in this incident had been shot dead," said Sheila Miller, spokesperson for the Bend Police Department. Authorities stated that it was not immediately clear who had fired the fatal shot at the gunman, noting it could have been a passer-by.
Police confirmed that at least two additional victims were rushed to a local hospital, though their conditions remain unknown.
The Bend-La Pine School District quickly confirmed the situation was under control, with pupils evacuated by bus to a nearby reunification site to be reunited with their families.
"We are shocked and heartbroken by this senseless tragedy," said Steven Cook, superintendent of Bend-La Pine Schools. "We extend our deepest condolences to the families and to all those affected by this violence. There are no words that can adequately express the pain our community is going through."

sources.news_title: Gunman Kills Teacher, Three Children In US School Shooting
sources.text:
A teenager shot and killed three children and a teacher on Thursday at an elementary school in the US state of Oregon, police said, adding the assailant was later killed by an armed bystander who pursued him into the building.
Officers rushed to Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, a city of about 100,000 in the nation’s northwest, after reports of a shooter on campus on Thursday afternoon.
The three children who died on the scene were aged five, eight and 11, said Bend police chief Mike Krantz. Another child and a teacher were being treated for critical injuries after the shooting.
The United States, where firearms are readily available, has a long and painful history of gun violence, with thousands of people killed every year. It has the highest rate of gun-related deaths among all developed nations.
People gathered in the city’s Drake Park on Thursday evening for a candelight vigil remembering the victims.
“I’m in total complete shock, and scared and sad,” said Betsy, who did not give her last name. She spent around 10 minutes contemplating a circle of candles and flowers.
“It’s awful, but it also has brought people together,” she told AFP.
Krantz, the police chief, told journalists that the department first learned of an active shooter after a call from a person who reported being shot at multiple times by a person carrying a long gun.
Dozens of emergency calls then reported that a shooter had entered the school and all law enforcement in the area were called to the scene, the chief added.
Officers arrived at 1:02 pm local time (2002 GMT) within minutes of the calls, he said.
“Moments later, an officer reported that the suspect had been shot by a community member who had seen the suspect enter the school and pursued him into the school and engaged him,” Krantz said.
“Our officers entered the building and confirmed the suspect was dead.”
One seven-year-old and one 54-year-old teacher with critical injuries were transported to a local hospital, he said.
The police chief said the investigation was in its early stages, but told the press conference it appeared “the shooter had forced their way into the school by shooting at locked doors.”
He added that the 16-year-old shooter was a Bend resident.
‘Unthinkable tragedy’
Between 400 and 450 children attend Silver Rail Elementary, where more than 40 staff work, according to a police spokesperson.
After a lockdown, Bend-La Pine School District said law enforcement was escorting students in buses to a separate location, where families could reunite with their children.
The district’s superintendent, Steve Cook, tearfully called the day’s events “an unthinkable tragedy.”
“We are heartbroken. We are horrified. This is the kind of thing you hear about in other places, and pray that it never happens here,” he told reporters.
Parents were anxiously waiting at the site near a church, where Drew Sharp, the father of a fifth grader, the highest grade in the school, told CBS News: “I have faith that he’s okay and that he’ll be alright.”
Children were disembarking from the bus youngest to oldest “which makes sense,” Sharp said, but “it’s just more time waiting.”
Friday classes at schools across the district along with activities and athletic events were canceled, Bend-La Pine said in a statement.
The elementary school is approximately 170 miles (270 kilometers) southeast of the city Portland. It serves primary-age students in kindergarten through fifth grade.
‘Cannot keep accepting this’
The deadliest school shooting in US history took place at Virginia Tech on April 16, 2007, when South Korean student Seung-Hui Cho killed 32 people and wounded 17 others before taking his own life.
There have been more than 360 mass shootings in the US so far this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive, which defines a mass shooting as four or more people shot.
“Our hearts are with the terrified children and the families anxiously waiting to hear that their loved ones are safe,” GIFFORDS, a gun safety organization, said on X.
“We cannot keep accepting this as a fact of life.”
Thursday’s shooting was followed by a painfully familiar chorus of calls for action on gun control, pleas that have resulted in little meaningful change.
In the face of decades of massacres, the powerful US pro-gun lobby has given millions of dollars to primarily conservative politicians in a successful bid to keep gun laws loose.
“They’re killing our babies. Shredding our kids with lead. Forcing us to live in fear,” said Janelle Bynum, an Oregon congresswoman, in a statement.
“This continues to happen,” she said later, speaking on CNN. “And it seems as if the adults don’t care.”
AFP

sources.news_title: DEADLY OREGON SCHOOL SHOOTING | What we know about the 16-year-old suspect
sources.text:
DEADLY OREGON SCHOOL SHOOTING | What we know about the 16-year-old suspect
BEND, Ore. (TNND) — A 16-year-old boy was identified as the suspect who killed three children and a teacher at an Oregon elementary school, police said, but authorities had not publicly named him or disclosed a possible motive as of Friday morning.
The teenager was fatally shot inside Silver Rail Elementary School on Thursday by a community member who saw him enter the building with a long gun, followed him inside and confronted him, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said.
"This is a terrible tragedy and we are working hard to investigate this incident and get as much information as possible out to the public," Krantz said.
"This is something we never want to happen anywhere, but especially and particularly in our beautiful community here in Bend," he added.
While officials did not name the bystander, his mother identified him as Kaylub Giamanco, a lifelong Bend resident who has two daughters at the school.
President Donald Trump said he was briefed on the shooting and praised Giamanco.
"There was a great hero and it could have been -- as bad as it was -- we had a great hero that went in and did the business," Trump told reporters outside the White House on Friday. "He took care of business. And thank God we had him, Otherwise, it would have been much worse. It's a terrible thing, but thank goodness for a man that had a gun and knew how to use it."
Police said the first 911 call came shortly before 1 p.m. from someone in a car outside the school who reported being shot at. Within minutes, dispatchers began receiving calls that a shooter had entered the school.
Krantz said the suspect forced his way inside by firing at locked doors. Officers arrived about three minutes after the first call and found him dead.
Authorities described the weapon only as a long gun. A law enforcement official briefed on the investigation told The Associated Press it was a pump-action shotgun bought by the suspect's mother.
Investigators also have not said whether the teen, who was a Bend resident, had attended Silver Rail, knew any of the people he allegedly killed, or had a connection to the school. They did not release information about a possible history of threats, disciplinary issues or warning signs.
Officials did not say whether the suspected shooter carried any other weapons, whether a note or digital evidence had been recovered, or whether he had prior contact with law enforcement before the attack in Bend.
The shooting killed three children ages 5, 8 and 11, as well as a teacher. A 7-year-old child and a 54-year-old teacher remained hospitalized with critical injuries, police said.
Children were taken by bus to a nearby church serving as a reunification center for families. Parents hugged, kissed and held their kids’ hands as they walked to their cars, with some bringing along favorite stuffed animals or other comfort items from home.
Bend-La Pine Schools Superintendent Steven Cook addressed families and staff after the shooting.
"Today, an unthinkable tragedy happened at Silver Rail Elementary School," Cook said. "You did what no one should ever be asked to do. I am so grateful beyond words for your efforts.
At a news conference, Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek said her heart was “absolutely broken” and thanked the civilian who pursued the shooter.
"To the community member who heroically intervened to stop further loss of life: Your actions carry a heavy emotional burden, and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well," she said.
The FBI is assisting Bend police, FBI Director Kash Patel announced on social media.
Classes and activities across the Bend-La Pine Schools district were canceled on Friday, as authorities continued to process the scene and interview witnesses.
The school in Bend, which is about 125 miles southeast of Portland, had 459 enrolled students as of last year, according to the Oregon Department of Education. The school serves students in kindergarten through fifth grade.

EDITOR'S NOTE: The Associated Press contributed to this report.

sources.news_title: Oregon School Shooting Kills Four; Teen’s Gun Access Investigated - FINCHANNEL
sources.text:
A 16-year-old gunman killed three children and a teacher at an elementary school in Bend on Thursday before an armed community member followed him inside and shot him dead, authorities said. The Oregon school shooting left another child and a teacher critically injured.
- Motive remains unknown: Investigators had not publicly established why the teenager attacked the elementary school. No verified finding about personal grievances, ideological motivation or the selection of particular victims was available in the reporting reviewed.
- Social media and warning signs: No authenticated account, manifesto or preattack post attributable to the suspect was identified in the reliable sources reviewed. Claims about bullying, previous threats or a psychiatric diagnosis remain unverified.
- Federal assistance: FBI Director Kash Patel said the bureau was assisting at the scene. ABC News also reported, citing a source, that Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives agents were heading to the school.
- School evacuation and family reunification: Officers cleared classrooms, and students were transported by school buses to Journey Church. Bend police identified the investigation as case number 2026-00057584.
- District closures: Classes, sports and extracurricular activities were canceled for Friday, October 16, across all 32 schools in the Bend-La Pine district.
- Support for children and families: Deschutes County was assembling mental health professionals to assist students and the wider community, Commissioner Phil Chang told Oregon Public Broadcasting. State emergency management officials said education, health and human services agencies were coordinating support.
- Questions still unanswered: The public record reviewed does not establish the weapon’s storage arrangements, any previous warnings to authorities, the suspect’s online activity, his relationship to the school or the precise sequence of shootings inside. Investigators have not publicly announced findings resolving those questions.
- KATU — school security upgrades: KATU reports that Silver Rail received classroom-door hardware upgrades in 2022. The district’s description says the locks could be secured from inside classrooms and remained locked when doors closed. The report does not establish whether those classroom doors were breached during the attack.
- Next police briefing: Officials planned another news conference Friday afternoon, October 16. KATU also reports that crisis counselors would be available at Bend’s Central Library beginning at 9 a.m. local time.
- KTVZ — additional closures: Beyond the school district’s closure, Central Oregon Community College announced that all campuses and facilities would close Friday, with classes and operations canceled. KTVZ also published statements from local educators and elected officials.
- FOX 12/KPTV — investigation expected to last days: KPTV reports that investigators would remain at the school for several days. Its page retains earlier, incomplete information about the injured, while CNN and KATU identify them as a 7-year-old child and a 54-year-old teacher in critical condition.
- Shooter’s name, parents and online activity: None of the directly reviewed CNN or Oregon local reports names the teenager or his parents, authenticates his social accounts, or establishes a motive. The civilian’s possible status as a student’s father is the principal additional lead in CNN’s coverage; it remains unconfirmed publicly by police.
The children killed at Silver Rail Elementary School were 5, 8 and 11 years old. A 7-year-old student and a 54-year-old teacher were hospitalized in critical condition, Police Chief Mike Krantz said at an evening briefing. The attacker forced his way into the building by firing through locked doors, according to Reuters’ account of the police briefing.
Investigators had not publicly established a motive in the reports available Friday morning. Police identified the attacker as a 16-year-old Bend resident but had not released his name or established whether he had attended the school or knew anyone there.
The Associated Press reported that he used a pump-action shotgun purchased by his mother, citing a law enforcement official briefed on the investigation who was not authorized to discuss it publicly. How the teenager obtained the weapon, and how it had been stored, remained unanswered.
How the Oregon school shooting unfolded
The first emergency call arrived at approximately 12:59 p.m. Thursday, October 15. Someone reported that a man had fired into a car, according to a Bend Police Department incident notice. Reports of gunfire at the elementary school followed.
According to the CNN , dispatchers alerted law enforcement at 1 p.m., and police directed the school to lock down at 1:01 p.m. Officers arrived at 1:02 p.m. and reported that the attacker had been shot.
Krantz said the armed community member saw the gunman enter the school, followed him and engaged him in gunfire. Authorities had not confirmed that person’s identity or relationship to the school. An early emergency dispatch suggested the person might have been a pupil’s father, but police had not substantiated that detail.
Students and staff were transported to Journey Church for reunification with families. Classes across the Bend-La Pine district were canceled Friday, Oregon Public Broadcasting reported.
The CNN account described security measures already installed across the district, including controlled entrance vestibules, visitor screening, cameras and classroom locks that could be secured from inside. Police said the attacker fired through locked doors; the available reporting did not establish how far he traveled inside the building.
The weapon and the questions facing investigators
Federal law prohibits licensed dealers from selling rifles or shotguns to anyone under 18. The minimum age for other firearms, including handguns, is 21, subject to additional state restrictions, according to the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives.
An adult’s purchase of a firearm does not, by itself, establish how a minor later acquired it or whether the adult committed an offense. In Bend, investigators had not publicly detailed the purchase, any transfer to the teenager or the circumstances in which he gained access.
Oregon’s firearm storage statute generally requires a firearm outside an authorized person’s control to be secured with an engaged trigger or cable lock, in a locked container or in a gun room. It also addresses unauthorized access to keys and combinations. Penalties increase when a minor obtains an unsecured firearm and the owner knew or should have known that unauthorized access was possible.
Access to family weapons has figured prominently in earlier school attacks. A National Institute of Justice research summary cited an open-source database study in which 80 percent of people who committed K-12 mass shootings stole the firearm from a family member. That finding concerns the cases examined in that study; it does not establish what happened in Bend.
What state statistics measure
CNN counted the Bend attack as the 36th shooting on K-12 school grounds in the United States this year, according to the supplied report. That is CNN’s database analysis, rather than a federal count.
For state comparisons, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention publishes standardized firearm mortality data. These figures count deaths from firearm injuries—including homicide, suicide and accidental shootings—not shooting incidents, nonfatal injuries or school attacks alone.
Selected states in the CDC’s 2024 data illustrate the variation:
| State | Firearm deaths | Age-adjusted deaths per 100,000 people | 
|---|---|---|
| Mississippi | 810 | 28.0 | 
| Oregon | 663 | 14.2 | 
| Massachusetts | 287 | 3.8 | 
The CDC’s state mortality figures adjust rates for differences in population age. They do not account for every other difference between states and cannot, on their own, establish why rates vary or measure the effectiveness of a particular law.
Why teenagers commit violence
No publicly established explanation yet accounts for the Bend teenager’s actions. Government research on youth violence examines combinations of circumstances rather than a single cause.
The CDC identifies risk factors that include exposure to violence, poor behavioral control, substance use, family conflict and association with delinquent peers. It explicitly cautions that risk factors may be associated with violence without being direct causes. Its framework addresses youth violence broadly, rather than predicting which teenager will carry out a school attack.
Research on targeted school violence has also documented behavior before attacks. A Justice Department account of a 2019 Secret Service study reported that, among 41 school attacks examined from 2008 through 2017, 94 percent of attackers had exhibited concerning behavior at school, 77 percent at home or in the community, and 74 percent online. Those overlapping categories describe past cases, rather than a test that reliably identifies future attackers.
The National Institute of Justice says many school mass shooters communicated their plans or showed signs of crisis beforehand. Its research summary recommends assessing reported threats through teams that can arrange mental health care, involve police when warranted and follow up on the student’s circumstances.
Legal responsibility beyond the attacker
Earlier school shootings have produced prosecutions over adults’ conduct and access to weapons. In Michigan, James and Jennifer Crumbley were each sentenced in April 2024 to 10 to 15 years in prison following involuntary manslaughter convictions connected to their son’s killing of four students at Oxford High School in 2021, according to Oakland County prosecutors.
Those convictions arose from the evidence and law in that case. The available Bend reporting does not establish comparable conduct by the teenager’s mother.
Oregon law also provides a route for civil claims when a weapon obtained through a storage violation injures someone within two years, subject to statutory conditions and exceptions. The Oregon Health Authority explains that an injured party may sue the owner in those circumstances.
Preventive restrictions face constitutional scrutiny as well. In its 2024 United States v. Rahimi decision, the Supreme Court upheld the federal firearm prohibition challenged by a man subject to a qualifying domestic violence restraining order. The ruling permitted temporary disarmament when a court finds a credible threat to another person’s physical safety; it did not decide every question involving firearm restrictions or school violence.
Prevention before an emergency call
Oregon’s existing prevention tools include extreme risk protection orders. Under the state’s red flag law, family members, household members and law enforcement officers can petition a court to restrict weapon access when a person presents a danger to themselves or others. The available reporting does not establish whether anyone sought such an order involving the Bend teenager. doj.state.or.us
The CDC’s youth violence prevention guidance recommends secure firearm storage, mentoring, stronger relationships between students and school staff, social and emotional skills instruction, and access to mental health and support services. Its evidence review also emphasizes supportive family environments and intervention for young people already exposed to violence.
In Bend, investigators still had to establish why the teenager targeted an elementary school, whether anyone knew of his intentions and how he obtained the shotgun reportedly purchased by his mother.
The 2015 Umpqua Community College shooting killed nine people. Here is who the gunman was, what happened in the classroom and how the deadly attack ended.
The Umpqua Shooting: Nine Killed in Oregon’s Deadliest School Attack
The Umpqua Community College shooting on October 1, 2015, killed eight students and their instructor in a classroom near Roseburg, Oregon. Federal health officials describe it as the deadliest mass shooting in the state’s modern history.
The attacker was Christopher Sean Harper-Mercer, a 26-year-old student at the college. He died by suicide after being wounded in an exchange of gunfire with responding police, according to the FBI’s account. Ten people died, including the gunman.
What happened
Students had gathered for an introductory creative writing class when Harper-Mercer attacked. He fatally shot the instructor and eight fellow students, according to a federal review of the shooting and recovery efforts.
The FBI places the beginning of the attack at approximately 10:38 a.m. It records nine victims killed and seven wounded. Other government and news accounts give different injury totals, so those figures should not be treated as interchangeable.
Who was the shooter?
Harper-Mercer lived near the college with his mother, Laurel Harper. His father was Ian Mercer. These identities concern the 2015 Umpqua attacker and have no established connection to the teenager responsible for the October 2026 Silver Rail Elementary attack. time.com
He briefly entered Army basic training in 2008 but was discharged after failing to meet minimum administrative standards, an Army spokesman told ABC News. He did not complete basic training.
How he obtained the guns
Investigators recovered five handguns and a rifle at the college. Federal firearms officials said the weapons identified in their initial investigation had been purchased legally; some had been bought by Harper-Mercer or relatives during the preceding three years, ABC News reported.
Additional firearms were recovered from the apartment he shared with his mother. The initial count increased as investigators continued searching, illustrating how early accounts changed during the investigation.
How the attack ended
Responding officers confronted Harper-Mercer and exchanged gunfire with him. He was wounded, then killed himself, the FBI concluded. Early reports that police had killed him were superseded by the subsequent finding of suicide.
Because the attacker died at the scene, there was no criminal trial of him. The investigation continued, and authorities released extensive records in 2017. The FBI also maintains publicly accessible investigative files on the Umpqua shooting.

Teen kills 4 at Oregon school. And, DOJ sues California over alleged noncitizens

Section Branding
Header Content
Teen kills 4 at Oregon school. And, DOJ sues California over alleged noncitizens
Primary Content
Good morning. You're reading the Up First newsletter. Subscribe here to get it delivered to your inbox, and listen to the Up First podcast for all the news you need to start your day.
Today's top stories
A teenager opened fire at an elementary school in Bend, Ore., killing three children — ages 5, 8, and 11 — and a teacher, officials confirmed. A 7-year-old and a 54-year-old were hospitalized. A bystander killed the 16-year-old suspected shooter after following him into Silver Rail Elementary School, according to local officials. The suspected shooter has not been identified. Officials say he was a resident of Bend. He used a "long gun," which is similar to a rifle or shotgun, during the attack. His connection to the school — if any — remains unclear.
- 🎧 The teenage suspected shooter was able to enter the school by firing at locked doors, according to the Bend Police Department. NPR's Arezou Rezvani tells Up First that something she found interesting on the Bend-La Pine Schools website was its emphasis on security protocols. They said they have secure vestibules for sign-in, ID checks for visitors and electronic buzz-in systems, but none of these measures stopped the gunman. Rezvani says police arrived at the school within minutes after the shooting started, but an unidentified community member shot the alleged shooter soon after the officer arrived.
The Justice Department is suing California to stop the state from counting ballots that the government claims are from noncitizens. Three weeks before Election Day, the DOJ provided a flash drive containing the names of 20,000 people it suspected of being noncitizens on California's voter rolls to Los Angeles County's top voting official. The DOJ gave him 48 hours to investigate the names or face a lawsuit, which was filed yesterday.
- 🎧 California and many election experts doubt the administration's noncitizen voting claims, citing President Trump's history of misinformation around the topic and flawed data analysis that can produce false positives, NPR's Miles Parks says. With vote-by-mail ballots already sent out for upcoming elections, the DOJ is seeking to segregate ballots linked to these claims for investigation so they don't get counted. Parks says it would be surprising if the DOJ succeeds in this lawsuit, as the Constitution clearly states that states manage elections.
Trump administration lawyers will argue today at a federal appeals court that White House papers belong to Trump rather than the American people. The case could end up in front of the conservative-leaning Supreme Court. The White House's claim comes after a series of actions during Trump's second term that challenged the limits put on the president after the Watergate scandal. For some 200 years, presidents could personally decide what to do with the papers they created in office. Then, Congress established the Presidential Records Act following disputes with Richard Nixon. Until this year, every president has followed this records law. Six months ago, the Trump administration moved to invalidate it. The move came after Trump was indicted on obstruction-of-justice charges for allegedly possessing classified documents at Mar-a-Lago, although a federal judge dismissed the case for technical reasons and the Justice Department later dropped it after Trump won reelection.
Behind the story
by Monika Evstatieva, senior producer on NPR's Investigations team
It all began with a tip. A colleague of mine had a friend in Ann Arbor who needed help. When I called her, she told me her elderly mom had been walking through a mall when a salesperson approached her with an eye cream sample. She went into a store called Beauty Essentials in Ann Arbor, Mich., and came out with $5,000 in skincare products she didn't want, tried to refuse, and couldn't return. But, she said, it wasn't an isolated incident. She posted on Facebook and connected with more than 30 people with complaints about the store. She asked me to look into it.
And so began an investigation that took place over more than a year. My reporting partner, Caley Fox Shannon, and I found similar complaints all over the country. We followed the trail, and found a network of mall skincare stores that systematically targeted older adults and people with disabilities across the United States. There was a link between them: one company, the California-based Mazal Group.
Over the past year, we spoke with more than 50 people, including customers who say they were taken advantage of, their family members and former employees. We looked at state and federal court lawsuits, hundreds of online reviews and nearly 500 consumer complaints we got through Freedom of Information Act requests. We went to stores selling products from Mazal Group in Virginia, Maryland and California, as well as the company's Chatsworth, Calif., headquarters.
You can read about what we found in NPR Investigations' whole report here, watch our documentary or listen on Consider This.

sources.news_title: Shooter kills teacher, three children at Oregon elementary school
sources.text:
A teenager shot and killed three children and a teacher on Thursday at an elementary school in the US state of Oregon, police said, adding the assailant was later killed by an armed bystander who pursued him into the building.
Officers rushed to Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, a city of about 100,000 in the nation's northwest, after reports of a shooter on campus on Thursday afternoon.
The three children who died on the scene were aged five, eight and 11, said Bend police chief Mike Krantz. Another child and a teacher were being treated for critical injuries after the shooting.
The United States, where firearms are readily available, has a long and painful history of gun violence, with thousands of people killed every year. It has the highest rate of gun-related deaths among all developed nations.
People gathered in the city's Drake Park on Thursday evening for a candelight vigil remembering the victims.
"I'm in total complete shock, and scared and sad," said Betsy, who did not give her last name. She spent around 10 minutes contemplating a circle of candles and flowers.
"It's awful, but it also has brought people together," she told AFP.
Krantz, the police chief, told journalists that the department first learned of an active shooter after a call from a person who reported being shot at multiple times by a person carrying a long gun.
Dozens of emergency calls then reported that a shooter had entered the school and all law enforcement in the area were called to the scene, the chief added.
Officers arrived at 1:02 pm local time (2002 GMT) within minutes of the calls, he said.
"Moments later, an officer reported that the suspect had been shot by a community member who had seen the suspect enter the school and pursued him into the school and engaged him," Krantz said.
"Our officers entered the building and confirmed the suspect was dead."
One seven-year-old and one 54-year-old teacher with critical injuries were transported to a local hospital, he said.
The police chief said the investigation was in its early stages, but told the press conference it appeared "the shooter had forced their way into the school by shooting at locked doors."
He added that the 16-year-old shooter was a Bend resident.
- 'Unthinkable tragedy' -
Between 400 and 450 children attend Silver Rail Elementary, where more than 40 staff work, according to a police spokesperson.
After a lockdown, Bend-La Pine School District said law enforcement was escorting students in buses to a separate location, where families could reunite with their children.
The district's superintendent, Steve Cook, tearfully called the day's events "an unthinkable tragedy."
"We are heartbroken. We are horrified. This is the kind of thing you hear about in other places, and pray that it never happens here," he told reporters.
Parents were anxiously waiting at the site near a church, where Drew Sharp, the father of a fifth grader, the highest grade in the school, told CBS News: "I have faith that he's okay and that he'll be alright."
Children were disembarking from the bus youngest to oldest "which makes sense," Sharp said, but "it's just more time waiting."
Friday classes at schools across the district along with activities and athletic events were canceled, Bend-La Pine said in a statement.
The elementary school is approximately 170 miles (270 kilometers) southeast of the city Portland. It serves primary-age students in kindergarten through fifth grade.
- 'Cannot keep accepting this' -
The deadliest school shooting in US history took place at Virginia Tech on April 16, 2007, when South Korean student Seung-Hui Cho killed 32 people and wounded 17 others before taking his own life.
There have been more than 360 mass shootings in the US so far this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive, which defines a mass shooting as four or more people shot.
"Our hearts are with the terrified children and the families anxiously waiting to hear that their loved ones are safe," GIFFORDS, a gun safety organization, said on X.
"We cannot keep accepting this as a fact of life."
Thursday's shooting was followed by a painfully familiar chorus of calls for action on gun control, pleas that have resulted in little meaningful change.
In the face of decades of massacres, the powerful US pro-gun lobby has given millions of dollars to primarily conservative politicians in a successful bid to keep gun laws loose.
"They're killing our babies. Shredding our kids with lead. Forcing us to live in fear," said Janelle Bynum, an Oregon congresswoman, in a statement.
"This continues to happen," she said later, speaking on CNN. "And it seems as if the adults don't care."

sources.news_title: Three children and a teacher shot dead at primary school in US
sources.text:
Details have emerged of the attack on a primary school, which saw three children and a teacher killed by a teen shooter.
The community in Bend, Oregon, is mourning the deadly shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School.
A gunman first struck outside the primary school shortly before 1pm local time yesterday after reports of a person in a car being shot at with a long gun.
Then, chilling 911 calls began to flood in, saying the shooter had entered the school, which has more than 400 pupils and over 40 staff.
Three children, aged five, eight, and 11, and an adult teacher were gunned down after the suspect, a 16-year-old male named Griffin J. John II, opened fire.
In a press conference later tonight, police explained that the assailant entered the building and fired as many as 15 rounds, including in the special education classroom, killing all three children inside.
Superintendent Steve Cook confirmed that the gunman was once a student at Silver Rail Elementary, which may be how he managed to bypass security.
Chief Mike Krantz added that he approached via a vacant side lot, jumped a playground fence, and shot through the locks on a side door.
Investigators are still looking into how he gained access, since the 11-year-old building was designed to prevent such attacks.
‘Rest assured, we will take a hard look at everything we have done,’ said Cook.
Officials said he was killed by a heroic armed bystander, who rushed in with a handgun.
A teacher also bravely intervened, tackling the teenager and helping to save lives.
She threw her phone at him and attempted to wrestle his gun from him, launching herself ‘on top of him’. Shockingly, she was not injured, but police declared she ‘almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed’.
When he was killed, the shooter had 44 more rounds of ammunition on him.
The teacher who died at the scene has been named as 25-year-old Meghan Lambert. In a statement, her family said this had been her first full-time teaching role.
‘She loved Silver Rail. This was her dream job.’
The five-year-old killed has been identified by his family as Rhoam Summer. Relatives of the other two child victims have asked that they not be identified at this time.
A seven-year-old pupil and a teacher, aged 54, were also critically injured and were taken to a local medical centre in Bend.
Bend Police said earlier: ‘At approximately 12.59pm, Bend Police responded to Silver Rail Elementary on reports of an active shooter. The first call indicated that an unknown man had shot into a car.
‘In the next minute, Deschutes County Dispatch received multiple 911 calls reporting that a person had entered the school and begun shooting.
‘Dispatch sent out an alert tone to send all law enforcement to the scene. At 1.02pm, Bend Police officers were on the scene. Seconds later, officers reported the suspect had been shot and killed, possibly by a bystander.’
Leah Schwartz, a resident walking near the school when the massacre started, said she heard at least six shots.
She told NBC: ‘They were spaced out, which made us question whether it was gunshots or someone doing construction.’
Officials have been tight-lipped about how the gunman got hold of the firearm, believed to be a long firearm, as an investigation continues.
In Oregon, people have to be 18 or older to buy rifles and shotguns, and 21 for handguns.
But legal loopholes exist, and minors can possess non-handgun firearms for activities like hunting or practice if they have parental consent.
The incident in Bend is the 36th shooting in an elementary and middle school this year alone, according to CNN, citing gun violence databases.
School shootings have been steadily increasing since 2008, with a surge in 2023 when a total of 84 school tragedies struck.
Gun violence and firearms are considered the leading cause of death for children and teenagers in the US, and thousands of people die in firearm-related incidents every year.
So far in 2026, a total of 361 people have been killed, and 1,553 people have been hurt across 365 mass shootings in the country.

sources.text:
A gunman was killed by a ‘heroic’ member of the public after leaving four dead in a school shooting in the US.

Just moments later, multiple calls were received that ‘a person had entered the school and begun shooting,’ according to a statement by Bend Police.
Upon entering the school, authorities quickly found that the shooter had already been killed by a community member who had seen and pursued them. The person behind this heroic intervention has yet to be identified.

sources.text:
A 16-year-old opened fire at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday, killing three children and a teacher before being shot dead by a community member, police said.
Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said in a press conference that the children killed at Silver Rail Elementary School were aged 5, 8, and 11. Also, a 7-year-old and a 54-year-old teacher were transported to St. Charles Bend hospital with critical injuries.
Krantz said the suspect, a male city resident who has not yet been publicly identified, was spotted entering the school by a community member, who eventually pursued him into the school and shot him. The chief said the suspect forced his way into the school by firing at locked doors.
Police did not speculate on the shooter’s motive and said they did not know whether the suspect knew anybody in the school or if he had attended.
FBI Director Kash Patel posted on social media that the agency’s Portland field office is assisting in the investigation. “We will make every resource they need available,” he added.
A vigil was held Thursday evening in the wake of the shooting.
“A school should be a safe place where children can learn and feel secure,” Bend Mayor Melanie Kebler said at the same press conference the police chief spoke at. “What happened today should never happen.”
Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek said at the same conference that her heart was “absolutely broken” over the incident: “No parent should have to have this kind of day, and no community should have to live through this kind of day.” She also thanked the community member who pursued the shooter.
CNN’s analysis of incidents reported by the Gun Violence Archive, Education Week and Everytown for Gun Safety shows that the shooting at Silver Rail Elementary marks the 36th one on K-12 school grounds this year. It is the 52nd school shooting in the country this year.
What happened?
Krantz said that at 12:59 p.m., police received a 911 call from a person in a vehicle who reported being shot at multiple times by someone “with a long gun.”
Multiple calls followed, reporting that a shooter had entered Silver Rail Elementary School, which is about 120 mi. southeast of Portland. The school enrolls more than 400 students from kindergarten to 5th grade.
Krantz said police directed the school to go into lockdown at 1:01 p.m. and first responding officers arrived a minute later. Upon entering the school building, Krantz said, officers confirmed that the suspect was dead and found the four other people who died from their injuries, and their families have been notified.

This has to end.”

Plans to help UK households save hundreds of pounds on their energy bills using plug-in batteries are a step closer, The i Paper can reveal.
New power banks
Although new power banks will be available to purchase from retailers, households will have to wait until 2028 to be able to install them due to pending safety checks.

Why the budget weekend away to Spain and Portugal could be over
Budget holidays to Spain and Portugal could become a thing of the past for Britons.
Soaring fuel prices
As the aviation industry enters its first winter since the outbreak of the US-Iran war, record-high fuel costs have led to airlines calling off hundreds of thousands of flights.

Expanding the licence fee
The plan is to extend the licence fee to platforms including Netflix and YouTube to prevent people from avoiding it by logging on to the internet via their phones, tablets or laptops, according to reports.
A White Paper on the BBC’s charter renewal is expected to be published before Christmas, which will set out how the corporation will be governed, regulated and funded from 2028 onwards.
The situation right now
- Currently, the TV licence is legally required to watch or record television on any channel or watch live TV on any streaming services, including BBC iPlayer.
- The fee rose to £180 on 1 April, but income from it has dropped by over £1bn in real terms over the past decade.

Much-discussed changes
It comes after The i Paper reported earlier this year that the BBC was looking to overhaul its funding model due to declining income and had suggested extending the licence fee to anyone streaming content on services like Netflix, Amazon, Disney, Apple and YouTube – who are currently exempt from the fee – whether the programming is live or on demand.

By Alanna Durkin Richer, Eric Tucker and Gene Johnson
Associated Press
BEND, Ore. — A 16-year-old shot his way through locked doors to get into an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday, killing three children and a teacher. He was then shot by a person at the scene who followed him inside, authorities said.
The suspect was found dead inside the school minutes after the shooting was first reported, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said.
The three children killed were aged 5, 8 and 11. Another child, 7, and a teacher, 54, were injured and taken to the hospital in critical condition, he said.
| WEBINAR: Ready before the call — Building a stronger fire and EMS preparedness strategy
The first 911 call came just before 1 p.m. from a person in a vehicle outside Silver Rail Elementary who reported being shot at by someone with a long gun, Krantz told reporters. Further 911 calls came from inside the school, and officers arrived on scene within minutes, police spokesperson Sheila Miller said.
The attacker, who police identified as a Bend resident, was shot and went down inside the school shortly after officers arrived, she said.
Police said they did not know if the shooter knew anyone at the school or whether he had attended.
Children were taken by bus to a nearby church serving as a reunification center for families. Parents hugged, kissed and held their kids’ hands as they walked to their cars, with some bringing along favorite stuffed animals or other comfort items from home.
The school in Bend, which is about 125 miles (200 kilometers) southeast of Portland, had 459 enrolled students as of last year, according to the Oregon Department of Education. The school serves students in kindergarten through fifth grade.
The high-desert city has ballooned in population over the past three decades and is a tourism and outdoor recreation hub near Mount Bachelor.
Classes, sports and extracurriculars were canceled Friday for all 32 schools in the Bend-La Pine district.
The shooting was the 28th mass killing in the U.S. this year, according to a database maintained by The Associated Press and USA Today in partnership with Northeastern University.
The attacker used a pump-action shotgun that was purchased by his mother, according to a law enforcement official briefed on the shooting. The official spoke to The Associated Press on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to publicly discuss the investigation.
At a news conference, Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek said her heart was “absolutely broken” and thanked the civilian who pursued the shooter.
“To the community member who heroically intervened to stop further loss of life: Your actions carry a heavy emotional burden, and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well,” she said.

sources.news_title: Bend, Oregon elementary school shooting: 3 children, 1 teacher killed; teen suspect dead
sources.text:
Bend, Oregon, school shooting: Suspect ID'd, previously attended elementary school, police say
The mass shooting at a Bend, Oregon, elementary school on Thursday that left three children and one teacher dead took place inside a special needs classroom, authorities said at a news conference, identifying some of the victims and the suspected shooter.
Three boys, ages 5, 8 and 11, and the teacher died at the scene, police said. At a news conference on Friday, authorities identified the teacher as 25-year-old Meghan Lambert, and one of the boys as 5-year-old Rhoam Summer. The names of the other two children killed are not being released at the request of their families, police said.
The suspected shooter, a 16-year-old armed with a twelve-gauge shotgun, was fatally shot by a community member who saw the teen going into the Silver Rail Elementary School and pursued him inside, according to Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz.
In another "heroic" act that may have saved lives, he said another teacher tackled the shooter to the floor and tried to take the gun away from him.
A 7-year-old girl and a 54-year-old teacher were wounded in the gunfire and were taken to the hospital with critical injuries, police said. The child was in serious but stable condition on Friday, and the teacher -- identified by her family as Becky Drury -- suffered serious but non-life-threatening injuries, police said.
Police identified the suspected shooter on Friday as Griffin J. John II, a Bend resident who formerly attended Silver Rail Elementary School. The suspect had been a special needs student at the school, school officials confirmed. He was not currently enrolled in the school district, according to the police chief.
Preliminary information indicates the 16-year-old suspected shooter used a pump-action shotgun believed to be purchased by his mother, multiple sources told ABC News.
"How the suspect got the weapon and ammunition remains part of the active criminal investigation, and I will not be able to address any of that portion today," Krantz said at a press briefing on Friday.
A motive also remains under investigation, police said.
"It will require substantial investigative time to continue that, but that is the answer we're seeking as well," Krantz said. "We may never get that full answer, but we want it."
How the shooting unfolded
The incident began unfolding shortly before 1 p.m. PT Thursday, police said.
At 12:59 p.m., police received a call from a driver who reported being shot at multiple times by a person with a long gun, the police chief said. The vehicle was struck three times.
Shortly afterward, the Deschutes County dispatch center began receiving multiple 911 calls that a shooter had entered Silver Rail Elementary School. The school was directed to go into lockdown at 1:01 p.m, Krantz said.
The shooter "forced" his way inside the school by shooting at the glass panes of locked doors multiple times, according to the police chief.
"The suspect went directly into the classroom, immediately to the left of the entry doors, where he fired as many as 15 rounds overall," Krantz said.
Officers arrived on the scene at 1:02 p.m., police said.
All of the shooting victims were located in that special needs classroom, he said. The suspect was also shot in the classroom and died at the scene, he said.
A Maverick 88 pump-action 12-gauge shotgun was located near the suspect, who had approximately 44 remaining rounds of 12-gauge ammunition, according to the chief.
Bystander 'heroically intervened,' governor says
Police said the shooter was fatally shot inside the classroom by a 36-year-old community member who had seen the teen firing at the truck and then followed him into the school, Krantz said.
His family on Friday identified him as Kaylub Giamanco, a father with two daughters who attend Silver Rail Elementary School.
Giamanco -- a lifelong Bend resident -- was driving near the school when he heard the commotion and ran inside, according to his family, who said he regrets not being able to save more lives. His family confirmed he has a concealed carry permit.
"He is not seeking recognition, but instead wishes to express his gratitude to the first responders, school personnel, and community for the outpouring of love and support," the Giamanco family said in a statement.
Police also commended another teacher who threw her cellphone at the shooter after he entered the classroom. The police chief said the teacher then "tackled him and fought to take the firearm from him," and that she "almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed." The police chief did not identify the teacher, and noted that she was uninjured.
Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek thanked teachers, staff and first responders who rushed to the scene and thanked the community member who she said "heroically intervened to stop further loss of life."
'We are heartbroken'
Following the shooting, police said they evacuated the school room by room. A reunification site for families was set up at a nearby church.
Bend-La Pine Schools Superintendent Steven Cook called the shooting an "unthinkable tragedy" and said, "We are heartbroken. We are horrified."
Thousands of community members gathered for a candlelight vigil Thursday night at Drake Park in Bend. A makeshift memorial has also grown outside the elementary school, with mourners leaving flowers, candles, toys and stuffed animals.
Kotek ordered flags at Oregon public institutions to be flown at half-staff on Friday from sunrise to sunset in remembrance of those who lost their lives at Silver Rail Elementary School.
Classes, activities and athletic events at all Bend-La Pine Schools were canceled Friday, school officials said.
"A school should be a safe place where children can learn and feel secure. What happened today should never happen," Bend Mayor Melanie Kebler said at Thursday's press briefing. "Like so many in our community, I'm struggling to make sense of a loss that feels unimaginable."
Large police response
A school resource officer was not at the elementary school at the time of the shooting, a police spokesperson said, noting that he officer oversees multiple schools and was at a nearby campus at the time.
The shooting sparked a large police presence as law enforcement and first responders raced to the school. Over 150 law enforcement officers and first responders have been involved in the investigation, police said.
"Everything they were doing seemed highly trained and highly prepared for this," Caleb Weis, who was riding his motorcycle near the school at the time, told ABC News.
"I didn't see as many phones out recording as you see on many other occasions, just a kind of a shock factor and an immense amount of respect for the law enforcement, first responders," he said.
FBI Director Kash Patel said the agency was on the scene assisting in the investigation. Agents with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives were also responding, according to a source.
Some parents who heard the sirens came to the school and anxiously awaited information.
"There's really no way to prepare for something like this," one father told ABC Bend affiliate KOHD.
ABC News' Alyssa Pone and Lisa Sivertsen contributed to this report.
This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

Once again, America is left grieving after a senseless act of violence targeted the most vulnerable among us: schoolchildren. Bend, Oregon: A 16-year-old boy opened fire at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, killing three children and a teacher before he was shot by a bystander who pursued him into the school, authorities said.
Authorities found the suspect dead inside the school on Thursday afternoon (Oregon time) minutes after the shooting was first reported, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said.
The three children killed were aged 5, 8 and 11. Another child, 7, and a teacher, 54, were injured and taken to a hospital in critical condition, Krantz said.

And as we learn more about the children and the adults who have been killed or injured, and their families and their loved ones, we are going to do a lot of crying, and we are going to cry together, and we're probably going to cry privately," Kotek said.
Krantz said the community member, whom he did not identify, saw the suspect enter the school and pursued him.
School shootings have become a recurring feature of American life, including high-profile attacks such as those at Columbine High School in 1999, Sandy Hook Elementary School in 2012, Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in 2018, and Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, in 2022.
Each shooting revives debates over gun laws in a country where gun rights are protected under the Constitution's Second Amendment. Gun rights advocates have argued for arming teachers as a means of defense.
Police trained for a mass shooting, Oregon governor says
Krantz said every Bend police officer went through a full day of active shooter training in August.
"Unfortunately, this is something we train for on a regular basis, and we must," Krantz said. "This is going to be a long investigation."

Silver Rail Elementary School serves kindergarten through fifth grade, roughly ages 5 to 11, and has about 450 students and 40 staff members, officials said.

Emergency responders received a call at 12:59 p.m. from a person in a vehicle who reported being shot at multiple times by someone with a long gun, Krantz said.
In the minutes afterward, dozens of calls were received saying the shooter had entered the school, Krantz said. Law enforcement immediately directed the school to go into lockdown, he said.

sources.news_title: Children Among Dead In Oregon Elementary School Shooting, Bystander Takes Out Gunman
sources.text:
At least four people, including three children, were killed Thursday afternoon in a shooting at an elementary school in central Oregon. The gunman is also dead.
Police said the 16-year-old male suspect opened fire on a vehicle with a long gun outside Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend before entering the building. Authorities said he forced his way into the school by shooting at locked doors. An armed Good Samaritan intervened before police arrived, killing the teenager inside the school. A responding officer said the community member saw the suspect enter the school, pursued him inside, and engaged him.
The three children killed were ages five, eight, and 11. An adult teacher was also killed, according to police. At this stage of the investigation, law enforcement does not know if the gunman had any connection to the school.
The horrifying ordeal appeared to unfold and end within minutes, thanks to a heroic bystander who stopped the shooter in his tracks, even as police responded swiftly.
“We received the first report at 12:59 of a shooter outside of the building shooting into a car, and within about a minute, we were receiving multiple 911 calls from within the school. Our officers were on scene at 1:02, and the shooter was down seconds later,” Sheila Miller, Bend Police Department’s communications manager, told local media.
During an evening briefing, police declined to specify the type of long gun used in the shooting or the number of rounds fired.
Oregon’s Democratic Gov. Tina Kotek said her heart is “broken” and praised the Good Samaritan who jumped into action.
“And to the community member who heroically intervened to stop further loss of life, your actions carry a heavy emotional burden, and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well,” she said.
FBI Director Kash Patel said federal agents are on the scene. “We will make every resource they need available,” Patel said in a statement.
Bend, about a three-hour drive from Portland, has nearly 100,000 residents. Silver Rail is a public K-5 school serving 438 students.
A reunification center was organized at a local church. Police urged the public to avoid the area. Another media briefing is scheduled for Friday.
“It’s devastating,” Miller told reporters, wiping away tears. “Apologies, it’s devastating, and our hearts go out to this community, and we ask our community to really work together and come together at this time.”
This is a developing story.

Teen shooter kills 3 children, teacher in Oregon.
A shooting occurred at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, resulting in multiple fatalities. According to coverage in NBC News and CNN, a teen shooter killed three children and a teacher before being shot by a bystander.
What happened
A school shooting occurred at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, where a teen shooter killed three children and a teacher before being shot by a bystander. This incident marks a tragic event in the ongoing discussion surrounding school safety and gun violence in the United States.
The shooter was identified as a teenager, but further details about the individuals involved have not been disclosed. The local community and authorities are responding to the aftermath of this devastating event.
Key facts
- A shooting occurred at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon.
- The incident resulted in the deaths of three children and one teacher.
- The shooter, a teenager, was killed by a bystander.
- Local authorities are investigating the shooting.

3 Children Died: All You Need to Know About Oregon Elementary School Shooting
- A teenage gunman forced entry into Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon on Thursday, killing three young children and an adult teacher
- A community member who witnessed the attack pursued the suspect into the school building, fatally shooting him before police arrived
- A 7-year-old child and a 54-year-old teacher were rushed to hospital with critical injuries as authorities launched a wide investigation
PAY ATTENTION: Mark Legit.ng as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed!
Three children and a teacher died on Thursday after a 16-year-old gunman opened fire at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, in an attack that ended when an armed community member chased the suspect into the building and shot him dead.
Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said at an evening press conference that Deschutes County dispatch received its first call at 12:59 p.m. local time from someone in a vehicle who said they were being fired upon by a person carrying a long gun. Within minutes, dozens of additional 911 calls flooded in as the shooter broke through the school's locked doors. A tone alert went out to all local law enforcement at 1 p.m., and the school was ordered into lockdown one minute later.
Officers reached the scene at 1:02 p.m., only three minutes after that first call, and quickly discovered that an unidentified community member had already engaged and killed the suspect. That individual had witnessed the gunman enter the school and chose to pursue him inside. Oregon Governor Tina Kotek later praised the unnamed person, saying they had "heroically intervened to stop further loss of life."
US shooting: Victims and the injured
The three children who died were aged 5, 8 and 11. An adult teacher also lost their life. Krantz confirmed that the families of all four victims had been notified, though none of the victims were publicly named. A 7-year-old child and a 54-year-old teacher were taken to St. Charles Medical Centre in Bend with critical injuries.
Silver Rail Elementary serves students from kindergarten through grade five and has more than 400 students and over 40 staff members. Officials did not say how far into the building the shooter advanced before he was stopped.
US elementary school shooting: Investigation under way
Authorities identified the suspect only as a 16-year-old Bend resident and did not disclose his name. Police said they had not yet confirmed whether he had any prior connection to the school. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives ran an urgent trace on the long gun used in the attack, and results were received Thursday evening, according to a source close to the investigation. How the teenager gained access to the weapon remains unclear.
Under Oregon law, individuals must be at least 18 to purchase rifles and shotguns. Minors may legally possess such firearms with parental consent for activities like hunting or target practice.
Krantz said a large law enforcement presence would remain at the school for several days, adding: "This is going to be a long investigation."
All schools in the Bend-La Pine Schools district cancelled classes and activities on Friday. Bend Mayor Melanie Kebler called it an "awful day for our community," saying a school "should be a safe place where children can learn and feel secure."
Obama grieves as family dog dies
Legit.ng earlier reported that Barack Obama announced the death of the family's Portuguese Water Dog Sunny, who had been with them since 2013.
Obama described Sunny as 'pretty much perfect', recalling how she bounded over hedges on the White House South Lawn.
Former White House photographer Pete Souza paid tribute to Sunny, noting her rare place in history.

sources.text:
3 Children, 1 Teacher Killed in Shooting at Bend, Oregon, Elementary School, Police Say; Suspect Dead
By Jordan Freiman, Sarah N. Lynch, Faris Tanyos, Camilo Montoya-Galvez, Anna Schecter, Pat Milton, Nicole Sganga
Three children and a teacher were killed, and two others critically wounded, in a shooting on Thursday at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, authorities said.
The suspect, a 16-year-old male, was shot and killed by a bystander, Bend police said.
Along with the teacher, the three children killed were ages 5, 8 and 11, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said in a news conference Thursday night. Two others, a 7-year-old child and a 54-year-old teacher, were taken to St. Charles Medical Center with critical injuries. No names were immediately released.
Krantz said that officers were called to the school just before 1 p.m. on a 911 call from a person who said they had been shot at several times while in their vehicle by a suspect with a long gun. Emergency dispatchers then received dozens of 911 calls that the suspect had entered the school.
The shooter forced his way into the school by “shooting at locked doors,” Krantz said.
When officers arrived at the school within three minutes of the first 911 call, they discovered that the suspect had been killed by a bystander, Krantz said.
“An officer reported that the suspect had been shot by a community member who had seen the suspect enter the school and pursued him into the school and engaged him,” Krantz told reporters.
After officers entered the building, Krantz said, they found the four deceased victims.
Officials would not say exactly what type of weapon was used in the attack or how many rounds were fired. Multiple law enforcement sources told CBS News the suspect used a shotgun, and The Associated Press cited a law enforcement official briefed on the incident as saying it was a pump-action shotgun purchased by his mother.
There was no word on a motive. Police could also not say if the suspect had a connection to the school. No details were provided on the bystander who shot and killed the suspect.
Authorities evacuated the school and transported all students and staff to a nearby church where they could be reunited with their families, Krantz said.
“Today an unthinkable tragedy happened at Silver Rail Elementary School,” Bend-La Pine Superintendent Steven Cook said in the news conference. “No community should have to do what we are doing right now. I don’t have any words for what this community is feeling right now.”
People gather outside Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, after reports of a shooting on Oct. 15, 2026.
FBI Director Kash Patel said the agency’s local office was on scene and assisting local law enforcement. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives was also on scene to assist local authorities, including the Oregon State Police, a law enforcement source said.
Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek praised the bystander who “heroically intervened to stop further loss of life,” saying the person’s actions carry “a heavy emotional burden.”
“All Oregonians mourn this loss today,” Kotek said in the news briefing. “This is a horrible day. No parent should have to have this kind of day. And no community should have to live through this kind of day.”
Bend-La Pine Schools said that all schools in the district would be canceling classes and athletic events on Friday due to the shooting.
Bend is located in central Oregon, about 150 miles southeast of Portland.
Last year there were 235 shooting incidents at K-12 schools in the U.S., according to data from the K-12 School Shooting Database. So far this year, there have been at least 149, including the one in Bend, Oregon. While still higher than pre-pandemic levels, school shooting incidents appear to be decreasing from a peak in 2023.
