sources.news_title: Four killed in US school shooting - News Today
sources.text:
Bend (Oregon), Oct 16:
Three children and a teacher were killed when a 16-year-old gunman opened fire at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday. The teenager was subsequently shot dead by a community member who confronted him inside the school, police said.
Two others, including a seven-year-old child and a teacher, were critically injured and taken to hospital. The victims who died included children aged five, eight and 11, along with a 54-year-old teacher, according to police.
The shooting occurred shortly before 1 pm local time, triggering a major emergency response. The first emergency call reported that a person with a firearm had shot at a vehicle near the school. Further calls soon alerted authorities that the suspect had entered the school and begun firing.
Police officers arrived within minutes and found the gunman dead from a gunshot wound. Police Chief Mike Krantz said a community member had followed the teenager into the school and engaged him with gunfire before officers reached the scene.
Investigators are examining how the teenager obtained the firearm and what prompted the attack. Authorities said the suspect was a local resident and that the investigation was continuing with assistance from federal agencies.
The shooting sent shockwaves through the local community, with families gathering near the school as emergency personnel secured the premises. Classes and activities across the Bend-La Pine school district were cancelled for the following day as the community began to deal with the aftermath of the tragedy.
The attack has renewed concerns over school safety and gun violence in the United States, where schools continue to face the threat of armed attacks.

sources.news_title: Three children, teacher killed in Bend elementary school shooting
sources.text:
Three children and a teacher were killed Thursday afternoon in a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, police said. The suspect, a 16-year-old Bend resident, was shot by a community member who saw him enter the school and went in after him.
The children killed were 5, 8 and 11 years old, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said at a press conference Thursday evening at Bend City Hall. A 7-year-old child and a 54-year-old teacher were taken by Bend Fire & Rescue to St. Charles Bend with critical injuries. The families of the victims have all been notified, Krantz said.
Police did not release the names of the victims or the suspect.
At 12:59 p.m., Deschutes County dispatch received a 911 call from a person in a vehicle who reported being shot at multiple times by a person with a long gun, Krantz said. Over the next several minutes, dispatch received dozens of 911 calls reporting that a shooter had entered the school on Southeast Stone Creek Lane.
Dispatch sent an alert tone to all law enforcement at 1 p.m. A minute later, officers responding to the scene directed the school to go into lockdown. The first officers arrived at 1:02 p.m., and moments later an officer reported that the suspect had been shot by the community member, Krantz said.
Officers went into the building, confirmed the suspect was dead and cleared the school of any other threats before giving emergency aid to the victims, he said. Officers found five people dead at the scene, including the suspect.
Answering a reporter's question, Krantz said the initial investigation shows the shooter forced his way into the school by shooting at locked doors. He said he did not yet know how far into the building the shooter got, whether the shooter knew anyone at the school, or what weapon the community member used.
Police would not say what kind of long gun the shooter used or how many rounds were fired.
Bend Police, the Deschutes County Sheriff's Office, Redmond Police, Oregon State Police, federal law enforcement and others evacuated the building room by room. Students and staff were taken on Bend-La Pine Schools buses to Journey Church on South Highway 97 to be reunited with their families, a process Krantz said was still going on Thursday evening.
"In August, every Bend police officer went through a full day of active threat training at a local high school," Krantz said. "Unfortunately, this is something we train for on a regular basis, and we must."
Police will have a large presence at the school for the next several days, he said.
"This is the kind of thing you hear about in other places and pray that it never happens here," Bend-La Pine Schools Superintendent Steven Cook said. "And it has happened here."
"To our staff who helped our students and protected our kids today, we thank you," Cook said. "You did what no one should ever be asked to do."
All Bend-La Pine schools are closed Friday, and all activities and athletic events are canceled, the district said. Crisis counselors will be at the Central Library starting at 9 a.m. Friday for students, families, district employees and anyone else in the community who needs support, Cook said.
"A school should be a safe place where children can learn and feel secure," Bend Mayor Melanie Kebler said. "What happened today should never happen."
Kebler said a community vigil was planned for Thursday night.
Gov. Tina Kotek opened her remarks by thanking Silver Rail staff, parents and first responders, and "the community member who heroically intervened to stop further loss of life."
"Your actions carry a heavy emotional burden, and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well," Kotek said.
Kotek said the Oregon Department of Emergency Management is coordinating across multiple state agencies. She said there will be time "for answering all those questions that we all have right now and searching for more ways to prevent this from happening in the future."
Kotek ordered flags at Oregon public institutions to be flown at half-staff from sunrise to sunset Friday in honor of the victims and survivors of the shooting, her office said Thursday evening.
Police have not said whether the shooter had attended Silver Rail. Sheila Miller, the Bend Police Department's communications manager, said officials plan to hold another press conference Friday afternoon.
Editor's note: This story is based on information from the Bend Police Department, Bend-La Pine Schools, the governor's office and the officials who spoke at Thursday evening's press conference in Bend. For the most accurate and up-to-date reporting, turn to Bend's local news outlets, including The Bulletin and The Source, TV newsrooms KTVZ and Central Oregon Daily, and OPB, which has a reporter covering Bend and Central Oregon. Their reporters cover Bend and will be covering the community long after national media moves on.

sources.news_title: Police: Active Shooter Situation At Bend Elementary School
sources.text:
Authorities Provide Update On Bend Elementary School Shooting Investigation
BEND, OR – Police say an active investigation continues after three children and a teacher were killed in a shooting at an elementary school in Oregon Thursday.
In a Friday update, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz noted the bravery of a teacher, and of a 36-year-old dad who has kids enrolled in the Silver Rail Elementary School where the shooting took place. Krantz said the dad shot his way through locked doors when he saw the shooter enter the school, then shot the now deceased 16-year-old male when he saw him wrestling with a teacher.
Krantz said the young student and teacher also wounded in the shooting are recovering in the hospital. The ongoing investigation includes determining how the shooter got his weapon.
ORIGINAL STORY:
BEND, OR – Police confirm three young children and one teacher died in the shooting at an elementary school in Bend today.
Officers responded to Silver Rail Elementary School after they received a call about a shot being fired into a car around 1 pm local time. Police say the suspected shooter is dead after being shot by a bystander who followed the shooter into the school and pursued him.
The suspect is identified as a 16-year-old male Bend resident.
Two other people, a teacher and a student, were taken to the hospital with critical injuries.
Governor Tina Kotek released the following statement in response to the shooting:
“I want to start by thanking and praising the quick thinking and courage of the Silver Rail Elementary School staff and parents – and the first responders who rushed to the scene.
And to the community member who heroically intervened to stop further loss of life, your actions carry a heavy emotional burden – and my thoughts are with you.
Almost exactly a year ago, I was at Silver Rail Elementary. I spent time with educators and community members calling parents to thank them for the great progress their kids were making in attending school. I heard the joy and excitement about their school.
My heart is absolutely broken. Our hearts will stay broken in the days and weeks ahead. My daily prayers will be with this community, with the children, with the parents.
All Oregonians mourn the loss of life today. This is a horrible day. No parent should have this day. No community should live through this day.
As we learn more about the children and the adult victims who died or were injured — and their families and their loved ones — we will weep together, and we will weep quietly to ourselves.
We must come together and support each other, neighbor to neighbor, Oregonian to Oregonian.
The Oregon Department of Emergency Management is coordinating across multiple state agencies, and the state stands ready to support the community in whatever it needs.
There will be time for answering all the questions we have and search for more ways to prevent this kind of violence from happening.
But for now, let us hold each other close in our grief, and put as much love into the world as possible.”
